nodes.title: Cell culture and neuronal differentiation
nodes.action: Culture neural stem cells Cor3-1 in Complete media with supplements and growth factors; induce neuronal differentiation by transferring cells to priming medium for 3 days, then to differentiation medium for 3 days with medium changes every 3 days and gradual reduction of FGF concentration
produces: Neural stem cells cultured and differentiated

nodes.title: Huwe1 knock-out via adenovirus transduction
nodes.action: Transduce neural stem cells (Floxed-Huwe1-RYFP) with adenovirus CMV-CRE at MOI 100 to induce Huwe1 knock-out; use empty adenovirus (CMV-null) at same MOI as control

nodes.title: P19 cell culture and differentiation
nodes.action: Maintain P19 cells in MEM-α with 10% FBS, penicillin and streptomycin; induce differentiation by transferring cells to Neurobasal medium supplemented with penicillin/streptomycin, 1% B-27 without vitamin A, GlutaMAX, and Laminin; change differentiation medium every 24 hours if required

nodes.title: P19 cell transfection with Lipofectamine 2000
nodes.action: Transfect P19 cells at 80% confluence with plasmid DNA using Lipofectamine 2000 in proliferation medium at a 1:2 DNA to Lipofectamine ratio following manufacturer’s instructions

nodes.title: Quantitative Real-Time PCR
nodes.action: Extract total RNA using RNeasy kit; synthesize cDNA using QuantiTect Reverse Transcription Kit; perform qRT-PCR using QuantiFast SYBR Green Master Mix in Lightcycler 480 PCR system with EiF1α as housekeeping gene; use specified thermal cycling conditions

nodes.title: Western blotting from total and fractionated lysates
nodes.action: Lyse cells with RIPA buffer with protease inhibitors or fractionated lysates; determine protein concentration with BCA assay; separate proteins by SDS-PAGE on 10% gels; transfer to nitrocellulose membranes; block with 10% non-fat milk in TBS-0.1% Tween; probe overnight with primary antibodies; incubate with secondary antibodies; develop membranes using ECL reagents
materials: primary antibodies (Ascl1, Histone H3, α-Tubulin, LaminB, Huwe1)
secondary antibodies (goat anti-mouse HRP, rabbit IgG HRP)

params.name: secondary antibody goat anti-mouse HRP dilution
secondary antibody rabbit IgG HRP dilution

nodes.title: Cellular fractionation of Cor3-1 and P19 cells
nodes.action: Seed cells; wash and pellet cells; sequentially lyse pellets with ice-cold E1 buffer with protease inhibitors and centrifuge to separate cytoplasm fraction; resuspend pellet in E1 buffer and centrifuge; resuspend pellet in E1 buffer and incubate on ice; centrifuge and discard supernatant; resuspend pellet in ice-cold E2 buffer with protease inhibitors and centrifuge to collect nucleus fraction; resuspend pellet in E2 buffer and centrifuge; resuspend pellet in E2 buffer and incubate on ice; centrifuge and discard supernatant; resuspend pellet in ice-cold E3 buffer with protease inhibitors; sonicate or digest chromatin fraction; centrifuge all fractions and determine protein concentration

nodes.title: Agarose-TUBEs pull down of ubiquitylated proteins
nodes.action: Use 15 μl of 50% Agarose-TUBEs to pull down 350-450 μg of ubiquitylated proteins from cytoplasm and chromatin fractions in 500 μl volume; incubate 1 hour at 4 °C on rocker; collect Agarose-TUBEs by centrifugation; wash 3 times; boil in reducing sample buffer; centrifuge and load eluted samples onto gels alongside unbound and input fractions

nodes.title: Grow tomato plants under controlled conditions
nodes.action: Germinate four-week-old tomato plants in vermiculite in a growth chamber under specified environmental conditions; irrigate seedlings twice a week with distilled water; irrigate seedlings for 3 weeks with Hoagland solution or modified nutrient solutions; adjust pH to 6.0 with 1mM KOH

nodes.title: Apply PA biosynthesis inhibitors and Put treatments
nodes.action: Prepare inhibitor solution containing 2mM DFMA and 5mM DFMO; apply inhibitor solution directly to each pot during the week prior to Pst inoculation; treat 4-week-old plants with 0.5mM Put or mock solution using foliar sprays 48h before Pst infection
produces: Plants treated with PA biosynthesis inhibitors or Putrescine

nodes.title: Culture and inoculate Pseudomonas syringae
nodes.action: Grow Pst and COR- strain in KB medium with rifampicin and kanamycin at 28 °C; prepare bacterial suspensions at 5×10^5 cfu/ml in sterile 10mM MgSO4 with 0.01% Silwet L-77; dip inoculate third and fourth leaves; score disease rate at 72h post-inoculation
produces: Inoculated tomato leaves with Pseudomonas syringae

nodes.title: Culture and prepare Botrytis cinerea spores
nodes.action: Culture B. cinerea on potato dextrose agar at 24 °C; collect spores from 10-15 day old cultures using sterile water with 0.01% Tween-20; filter, quantify with haemacytometer, and adjust concentration to 1×10^6 spores/ml

nodes.title: Measure biomass, chlorophyll content, and photosynthetic rate
nodes.action: Collect four-week-old tomato plants; dry tissues at 65 ºC for 2 days and weigh for biomass; measure chlorophyll content using SPAD meter with three measurements per leaf on 10 plants; measure net photosynthetic rate on three mature leaves per plant using LCpro+ infrared gas analyser under ambient CO2 and humidity with supplemental PAR lamp light

nodes.title: Determine H2O2 accumulation and perform microscopy
nodes.action: Collect 10 leaves for DAB staining at 3, 24, and 48 hpi; stain leaves in 1mg/ml DAB at pH <3 for 24h in dark; destain in 96% ethanol and rehydrate; quantify DAB staining intensity from micrographs using GIMP; quantify H2O2 using xylenol orange method from leaf discs floated on water, centrifuged, and reacted with assay reagent; incubate mixture 30min at room temperature; measure absorbance at 560 nm

nodes.title: Analyze gene expression by qRT-PCR
nodes.action: Extract RNA from leaf tissue at 3 and 48 hpi; digest RNA with RNase-free DNase; inactivate DNase; reverse transcribe RNA to cDNA; perform qRT-PCR with specific primers and SYBR Green detection; use EF1α as housekeeping control; perform melting curve analysis; calculate amplification efficiency; determine differential gene expression using cycle number differences

nodes.title: Analyze stomatal aperture by microscopy
nodes.action: Inoculate third and fourth leaves with Pst; collect leaves at 1 and 3 hpi; make epidermal impressions using dental resin and nail polish; image stomata by light microscopy; analyze stomatal aperture using Eclipse-Net software; measure approximately 50 stomata per leaflet

nodes.title: Conduct flagellar protein export assay
nodes.action: Grow Salmonella cells in 5 ml of LB with shaking at 30°C until OD600 ~1.0. Wash cells twice with motility buffer (10 mM potassium phosphate, 0.1 mM EDTA, pH 7.0). Resuspend cell pellets in motility buffer and incubate at 30°C for 1 hour. Centrifuge cultures to separate cell pellets and supernatants. Resuspend cell pellets in SDS loading buffer. Precipitate proteins in supernatants with 10% trichloroacetic acid, suspend in Tris-SDS loading buffer, and heat at 95°C for 5 min. Perform SDS-PAGE and immunoblotting with polyclonal anti-FlgD and anti-FliC antibodies.

nodes.title: Purify pHluorin(M153R) and pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His proteins
nodes.action: Purify pHluorin(M153R) from soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM007. Purify pHluorin(M153R)-FliG-His by nickel-nitrilotriacetic acid (Ni-NTA) affinity chromatography from soluble fractions of BL21(DE3)pLysS carrying pYVM013.

nodes.title: Fluorescence microscopy of Salmonella cells
nodes.action: Observe Salmonella cells expressing pHluorin(M153R), pHluorin(M153R)-FliG, pHluorin(M153R)-Flk, or pHluorin(M153R)-MinD MTS under a custom-built fluorescence microscope system. Use an inverted fluorescence microscope (IX-71; Olympus) with a 150× oil immersion objective lens (UApo150XOTIRFM; NA 1.45; Olympus) and 1.6× variable inserts. Excite pHluorin(M153R) probe with a xenon lamp using two excitation filters (400AF30 for 410-nm excitation and BP 470–490 for 470-nm excitation). Switch excitation filters with a high-speed wavelength switcher (Lambda DG-4; Sutter) at less than 2 ms switching speed. Capture fluorescence emission through a dichroic mirror and emission filter by an EMCCD camera (C9100-02; Hamamatsu Photonics) controlled by MetaMorph 3.6 software.

nodes.action: Expand primary human astrocytes in Human Astrocyte Media supplemented with fetal bovine serum, penicillin streptomycin, and Astrocyte Growth Supplement. Prior to experiments, culture astrocytes in a 50:50 mix of F10:MEMα media supplemented with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin streptomycin.

nodes.title: Reduce IGF1R levels in astrocytes
nodes.action: Treat astrocytes with 11 μg/ml IGF1R-specific monoclonal antibody MAB391 for 24 hours. After treatment, wash cells with 1× PBS and culture for a further 72 hours in fresh F10:MEMα media. Include IgG isotype control MAB002.

nodes.title: Culture and differentiate LUHMES cells
nodes.action: Grow LUHMES cells in proliferation medium containing DMEM/F12 GlutaMAX supplement medium, N2 supplement, and 40 ng/ml recombinant basic fibroblast growth factor (FGF). When cells reach 50–60% confluence, differentiate by replacing media with differentiation media containing 1 μg/ml tetracycline. After two days, trypsinize and replate cells for an additional three days to become fully differentiated.

nodes.title: Generate GFP LUHMES cells
nodes.action: Transduce non-differentiated LUHMES cells with GFP-expressing lentiviral particles (LV-GFP) for 24 hours. Replace media with fresh proliferation media and culture for an additional 72 hours before experiments.

nodes.title: Culture fibroblasts as control cells
nodes.action: Culture fibroblasts in Minimum essential medium supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% penicillin streptomycin, 1% MEM non-essential amino acids, 1% MEM vitamins, 1% sodium pyruvate, and 60 μg/ml uridine. Use fibroblasts as controls for neurite outgrowth specificity.

nodes.title: Set up astrocyte-LUHMES co-cultures
nodes.action: Seed astrocytes onto fibronectin (1 μg/ml)-coated 24-well plates at 30,000 cells/well. Add differentiation media to LUHMES in separate flask. After 2 days, replate LUHMES onto astrocytes at 7,500 cells/well and co-culture for 24 hours in differentiation media. Set up fibroblast-LUHMES co-cultures similarly with fibroblasts seeded at 50,000 cells/well.

nodes.title: Co-culture with MAB391-treated astrocytes
nodes.action: On day 1, seed astrocytes onto fibronectin-coated plates and add differentiation media to GFP-LUHMES in separate flask. On day 2, treat astrocytes with 11 μg/ml MAB391 or MAB002 for 24 hours. On day 3, replate GFP LUHMES onto treated astrocytes and remove antibodies. Maintain co-cultures in differentiation media for 72 hours, then treat with 50 μM H2O2 for 2 hours.

nodes.title: Prepare astrocyte lysates
nodes.action: After treatments, remove medium and wash cells with ice-cold PBS. Lyse cells in extra strong lysis buffer containing detergents and inhibitors. Incubate lysates on ice for 25 minutes, sonicate, and centrifuge at 17,000 g for 30 minutes at 4 °C. Determine protein concentration using BCA protein assay kit.

nodes.title: Grow Phaseolus vulgaris seedlings
nodes.action: Sow seeds in vermiculite and grow in a growth chamber at 23°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle and 75% relative humidity. Cultivate seedlings in plastic pots filled with moist vermiculite for 10–12 days until primary leaves are fully expanded.
produces: Phaseolus vulgaris seedlings at fully-expanded primary leaf stage

nodes.title: Transplant seedlings and dark adaptation
nodes.action: Transplant three seedlings into moist vermiculite in 20 cm plastic pots and place in a dark room 24 hours prior to inoculation.

nodes.title: Prepare viral vectors by cloning target gene fragments
nodes.action: Amplify P. vulgaris target gene fragments by PCR using specific primers and high fidelity polymerase. Digest PCR products with BamH1 and insert into BamH1-digested and dephosphorylated pBPMV-IA-V1 plasmid to generate VIGS vectors. For BPMV-PvPDS-52 bp, directly clone a double-stranded synthetic oligonucleotide into BamH1 site. Verify orientation of inserts by PCR and sequencing.
produces: BPMV-derived viral vectors for gene silencing

nodes.title: Prepare DNA-plasmid mix for primary inoculation
nodes.action: Prepare a 20 μL DNA-plasmid mix containing equal amounts of pBPMV-IA-R1M and either pBPMV-IA-V1 or pBPMV-GFP2 plasmids using 50 mM potassium phosphate buffer (mock buffer) at pH 7.0.

nodes.title: Perform mechanical rub-inoculation of plants
nodes.action: Place plants in the dark 24 hours prior to inoculation. For primary inoculation, mechanically rub the DNA-plasmid mix onto one primary leaf. For secondary inoculation, prepare leaf sap by grinding infected leaves in mock buffer and rub onto plants. Grow inoculated plants at 19°C under a 16 h light/8 h dark cycle.

nodes.title: Optimize rub-inoculation conditions
nodes.action: Test different DNA plasmid amounts (1.5, 3, or 5 μg) and rubbing intensities (low, medium, high) on P. vulgaris cv. Black Valentine plants at the fully-expanded primary leaf stage to optimize inoculation efficiency.

nodes.title: Visualize GFP expression in plants
nodes.action: Examine GFP expression in aerial organs and roots using a UV lamp and photograph with a digital camera. Perform microscopic observations of roots at 21 days post-inoculation using an Axioskop microscope and RT KE camera.

nodes.title: Generate QT6/ACE2 Cell Line
nodes.action: Clone human ACE2 gene from a human primary kidney cDNA library, subclone into pcdna3.1+, transfect QT6 cells using lipofectamine 2000, and select G418-resistant ACE2-positive cells.

nodes.title: Produce Viral Vectors
nodes.action: Transfect 293T cells with gag/pol, GFP reporter, and envelope constructs using Fugene-6. Harvest supernatant at 48 and 72 hours post-transfection, filter, and store at -80°C.

nodes.title: Measure Viral Vector Titer
nodes.action: Infect 293T, TE671, and QT6/ACE2 cells with viral vectors and determine eGFP titers 72 hours later by fluorescence-activated cell sorter (FACS) to quantify infectious units per milliliter.

nodes.title: Perform Live Virus Neutralization Assay
nodes.action: Heat-inactivate patient serum samples at 56°C for 30 min, serially dilute from 1:10 in culture medium, incubate with 50 PFU SARS Frankfurt strain virus for 1 h at 37°C, add 5 × 10^4 Vero E6 cells per well, incubate for 4 days, and assess neutralization by cytopathic effect (CPE).

nodes.title: Perform Pseudotype Neutralization Assay
nodes.action: Heat-inactivate patient serum samples at 56°C for 30 min, 2-fold serially dilute from 1:10 in culture medium, mix with MLV(SARS) virions (~100 IU) at 1:1 vol/vol ratio, incubate at 37°C for 1 h, add 100 μL of each dilution to QT6/ACE2 cells seeded at 1 × 10^4 cells per well in 96-well plates seeded 24 h previously, and count GFP-positive cells 48 h later by fluorescence microscopy.

Design probes from input sequences
nodes.action: Generate variable length probes (50-100 mers) at 5-bp steps from input sequences derived from gene models, full-length cDNA, and de novo assembled RNA-Seq contigs. Repeat-mask probes by removing those with average 15-mer frequency >200 and eliminate probes with more than 25 matches to target sequences. Select unique probes at average 40 bp spacing to create the probe set.

nodes.title: Hybridize array with barley cultivars
nodes.action: Hybridize two slides of the array design with four barley cultivars using standard CGH protocols for 4 days. Remove probes identified as missed repetitive elements based on high signal intensity and exclude contaminants or non-performing probes based on low signal for all cultivars. Use remaining probes to construct solution-phase capture pool.
materials: barley cultivars Steptoe, Barke, Morex, Bowman

nodes.title: Prepare Illumina TruSeq paired-end libraries
nodes.action: Fragment 1 μg genomic DNA into 200-300 bp size range using Covaris S220 instrument with 175 W ultrasonic power, 10% duty factor, 200 cycles per burst, 100 sec treatment time. Optionally size fractionate adapter-ligated products between 320 and 420 bp by excision from SYBR-Gold stained agarose gel. Purify libraries using AmPure XP Beads and elute in 30 μl Resuspension Buffer.
materials: Illumina TruSeq Paired End library kit

nodes.title: Perform pre-capture ligation-mediated PCR (LM-PCR)
nodes.action: Use 20 μl of TruSeq DNA library as template in 100 μl LM-PCR reaction containing Illumina sequencing adapters (2 μM TS-PCR Oligo 1 and 2 μM TS-PCR Oligo 2) and 50 μl Phusion High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix (2×). Perform LM-PCR cycling, clean-up and elution as described. Quantify DNA with Qubit 2.0 fluorometer and analyze fragment size electrophoretically with Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer using DNA 7500 chip. Confirm library fragments between 250 and 500 bp.

nodes.title: Prepare capture library with blocking oligos and enhancers
nodes.action: Add 10 μl Plant Capture Enhancer (PCE) to 1 μg amplified sample library. Add 1 μl 1 mM TS-HE Universal Oligo 1 and 1 μl 1 mM appropriate TS-INV-HE Index Oligo. Dry mixture in SpeedVac at 60°C. Pool up to six samples with different indexes proportionally to concentration. Add 7.5 μl 2× Sequence Capture Hybridization Buffer and 3 μl Hybridization Component A to dried sample. Vortex and centrifuge. Denature at 95°C for 10 min before hybridization.

nodes.action: Transfer denatured hybridization cocktail to PCR tube containing 4.5 μl Exome Library (liquid array). Incubate hybridization sample (15 μl) in thermocycler with lid heated to 57°C at 47°C for 64–72 hours.

nodes.title: Wash and purify captured DNA with Dynabeads
nodes.action: Prepare Streptavidin Dynabeads by vortexing and washing with Bead Wash Buffer. Bind hybridization sample to beads at 47°C for 45 min with intermittent vortexing. Wash beads sequentially with SC Wash Buffer I (pre-heated to 47°C), Stringent Wash Buffer (pre-heated to 47°C), and Wash Buffers I-III at room temperature with specified vortexing durations. Resuspend bead-bound captured library in 50 μl PCR-grade water.

nodes.title: Amplify bead-bound captured library by LM-PCR
nodes.action: Prepare 200 μl LM-PCR master mix containing 50 μl bead-bound captured library, 2 μM Illumina sequencing adapters (TS-PCR Oligo 1 and 2), and 100 μl Phusion High-Fidelity PCR Master Mix (2×). Distribute 100 μl master mix into two PCR tubes. Perform LM-PCR cycling: 98°C for 30 sec; 16 cycles of 98°C for 10 sec, 60°C for 30 sec, 72°C for 30 sec; final extension 72°C for 5 min; hold at 8°C. Combine reactions and purify using Qiaquick PCR purification kit with modifications. Elute DNA in 50 μl EB preheated to 50°C. Assess purity by A260/A280 ratio (1.7–2.0) and fragment size (250-500 bp) by Bioanalyzer.

Culture D. coniospora and extract genomic DNA
nodes.action: Culture D. coniospora spores in liquid NGMY medium for 7 days; harvest mycelia by vacuum filtering through 10 μm nylon membrane; dry mycelia at 30°C for around 3 h; grind mycelia in liquid nitrogen-cooled mortar; transfer 20 mg aliquot to 1.5 mL tube; extract DNA using DNeasy Plant Mini Kit following manufacturer’s instructions

nodes.title: Prepare samples and extract RNA from spores and mycelia
nodes.action: Collect fresh spores from 10 cm NGM plates of infected worms; inoculate in 100 mL NGMY liquid medium; culture either for 4 days or serially for 5 cycles of 8 days with agitation to disrupt mycelia; filter cultures through 0.22 μm Steritop units; flash freeze in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C; dissolve 200 mg aliquots in 1 mL Trizol in lysing matrix tubes; homogenize twice for 20 s at 6 m/s with 2 min ice incubation; purify RNA using standard protocol and clean with RNeasy mini Kit

nodes.title: Construct genomic DNA libraries and perform sequencing
nodes.action: Prepare MIseq paired-end libraries from genomic DNA and sequence on Illumina MIseq sequencer as 2 x 150 bp paired-end reads; prepare two mate-paired libraries for SOLiD sequencing from genomic DNA; shear DNA to 1.5 kb or 3 kb fragments using Covaris System and Blue miniTUBES; perform nick-translation for 9.5 min to generate fragments < 400 bp; amplify library with 14 rounds of PCR; size-select fragments between 250 and 300 bp using 4% acrylamide gel; purify with SOLiD Library Micro Column Purification Kit; convert libraries for analysis with 5500 WildFire system
materials: SOLiD Library Micro Column Purification Kit

nodes.title: Construct cDNA libraries and perform Illumina mRNA sequencing
nodes.action: Construct cDNA libraries from mRNA of spores and mycelia; sequence using Illumina HiSeq 2000 platform; obtain more than 48 million 90 bp paired-end reads from each 200 bp insert library

nodes.title: Perform de novo genome assembly
nodes.action: Process MIseq reads with BBDuk software to filter contaminants and low quality reads; assemble filtered reads de novo using Velvet, SPAdes, SOAPdenovo2, and ABySS with standard parameters except ABySS with k values 64 and 96; scaffold assemblies using SOLiD mate-paired reads with SSPACE v2.0 using k parameter 5

nodes.title: Perform de novo transcriptome assembly
nodes.action: Assemble combined reads from spores and mycelia mRNA sequencing libraries de novo into transcriptome using Trinity with default parameters

nodes.title: Generate optical genome map
nodes.action: Generate whole genome map of D. coniospora using Argus Whole-Genome Mapping System; select XbaI enzyme for size-optimized restriction fragments; sort molecules longer than 200 kb (average 310 kb); assemble with MapSolver software; manually validate resulting map contigs leading to 9 maps ranging 0.58 to 11.3 Mb with cumulative size 31.8 Mb; use maps for comparison with in silico XbaI digestion profile of scaffolds

nodes.title: Annotate genome for repetitive elements and non-coding RNA
nodes.action: Identify repetitive elements using RepeatScout; generate repeat library and mask genome with RepeatMasker; characterize transposable elements with TransposonPSI; identify non-coding RNAs using Rfam scan perl script and tRNAscan-SE
produces: annotated genome with repetitive elements and non-coding RNAs

nodes.title: Conventional ChIP-Seq Sample Preparation
nodes.action: Resuspend fixed cells (1.2 million FACS sorted NSCs per replicate) in 140 mM RIPA buffer; sonicate for 14 cycles with 30 sec ON/OFF at high settings using bioruptor; centrifuge at 14,000 g for 10 min at 4°C; incubate supernatant overnight with 2 μg specific antibody at 4°C with head-over-tail rotations; add 20 μl blocked Protein A and G Dynabeads and incubate 3 h; separate beads magnetically and wash sequentially with 140 mM RIPA once, 250 mM RIPA four times, and TE buffer twice; treat samples with RNase and Proteinase K for cross-link reversal; extract DNA by phenol–chloroform; dissolve DNA in 30 μl TE buffer; prepare sequencing libraries using NebNext Ultra II DNA library preparation kit
materials: NebNext Ultra II DNA library preparation kit

nodes.title: TAF-ChIP Sample Preparation and Library Construction
nodes.action: Fix cells with 1% formaldehyde for 10 min at room temperature; quench with 125 mM glycine for 5 min; wash cells with ice-cold PBS; sort cells directly into 240 μl 140 mM RIPA buffer; sonicate nuclei with 3 cycles at low power; couple 15 μl Protein A and G Dynabeads with 1 μg antibody in blocking buffer for 2-3 h at 4°C; centrifuge chromatin at 2,000 g for 10 min at 4°C and transfer supernatant to antibody-coupled beads; incubate overnight at 4°C with head-over-tail rotations; wash beads twice with 300 μl homemade tagmentation buffer; resuspend beads in 20 μl 1× tagmentation DNA buffer with 1 μl Nextera DNA tagmentation enzyme; incubate at 37°C for 40 min with shaking at 500 rpm; wash beads once with 140 mM RIPA, four times with 250 mM RIPA, and twice with TE buffer; treat samples with Proteinase K overnight at 60°C with shaking; either phenol–chloroform extract and precipitate DNA or heat-inactivate Proteinase K and directly PCR amplify; purify PCR products by bead-based size selection; analyze libraries by Bioanalyzer and Qubit; pool libraries and sequence
materials: blocking buffer (RIPA + BSA + glycogen + yeast tRNA)

nodes.title: CRISPR-Cas9 Genome Editing
nodes.action: Create GFP-tagged rad-51 and spo-11 mutations in worm strains using CRISPR-Cas9 with pDD282 plasmid, crRNA, and dyp-10 coconversion. Add GFP tag to N-terminus of RAD-51 and generate spo-11 deletions or insertions.
produces: GFP-tagged rad-51 and spo-11 mutant worm strains

nodes.title: Live Worm Imaging
nodes.action: Image live worms using MetaMorph software and Leica 100×/1.4 NA oil objective illuminated with 110LED. Set light source intensity to 5%. Use exposure times of 500 ms for GFP channel and 20 ms for D&C. Locate nuclei based on GFP fluorescence of tagged proteins. Perform time series imaging to monitor foci formation and dynamics after microirradiation.
produces: Live imaging data of fluorescent foci

nodes.title: Image Processing and Foci Scoring
nodes.action: Process live imaging stacks in MetaMorph to create maximum projections. Score nuclei for foci in FIJI-ImageJ. Count foci in microirradiated nuclei and adjacent nuclei as negative controls. Record size of foci; classify foci exceeding 0.6 μm diameter as focus clusters. Assess worm viability by monitoring foci movement and autofluorescence. Exclude nuclei when fluorescence is too diminished for scoring.
produces: Quantified foci counts and size data

nodes.title: Fixed Slide Imaging and Analysis
nodes.action: Image fixed slides using DeltaVision wide-field fluorescence microscope with 100×/1.4 NA oil Olympus objective. Deconvolve images with softWoRx software. Record gonad length and foci locations using cell width counts from distal tip cell. Analyze images with softWoRx Explorer software. Identify focus clusters as foci with diameter exceeding 0.6 μm.
produces: Analyzed fixed sample images with foci distribution data

nodes.title: Microirradiation of Germline Nuclei
nodes.action: Locate target nuclei in germline and focus Z-plane on center of nuclei. Microirradiate each nucleus with a single pulse using Andor micropoint 365nm pulsed laser attenuated in MetaMorph to specified percentage of total 80 μJ output. Target mid-pachytene nuclei at one pulse per nucleus for 5–7 nuclei per gonad. Adjust motorized optical attenuator to set laser power percentage. Recover worms immediately after microirradiation and dissect at appropriate time intervals.

nodes.title: Live Imaging Slide Preparation and Worm Recovery
nodes.action: Position worms on 3% agarose pads made with M9 or in live imaging petri dishes with M9 and 0.1-μm polystyrene beads. Seal petri dishes with Parafilm. After imaging and microirradiation, recover worms by submerging slides in M9 and removing coverslips or agarose pads. Place recovered worms on NGM plates seeded with OP50 until dissection.
produces: Prepared live imaging slides and recovered worms

nodes.title: Animal Housing and Food Restriction
nodes.action: House male 3-month old BALB/cARC and C57BL/6JARC mice in groups of four in individually ventilated caging with bedding under 12-h light cycle at 21 ± 1°C and 50 ± 10% humidity. Food restrict mice to 90% of free-feeding body weight by adjusting daily food amount; provide food at same time daily with ad libitum water.

nodes.title: Touchscreen Apparatus Setup and Habituation
nodes.action: Set up operant chambers equipped with touchscreen, house light, reward dispenser, and magazine inside sound-attenuating box with overhead camera. Place black 2-window (7.0 × 7.5 cm) mask in front of touchscreen. Clean mask, touchscreen, grid floor, and tray with 70% ethanol between animals. Flush reward lines with warm water and pump dry daily. Habituate mice in dimly lit (10% fluorescent lighting) testing room for minimum 30 min prior to each training session with house light off.

nodes.title: Touchscreen Training with Liquid Reward
nodes.action: Acclimate mice to liquid reward by providing strawberry milk in home cage in 50 ml falcon tube lid for 3 days prior to training. Progress mice through training stages: Habituation (collect reward when tray illuminated, complete 50 trials within 20 min on two consecutive sessions), Initial Touch (touch white square stimuli for 3× reward or single reward after 30 s no activity), Must Touch Stimuli (complete 100 trials within 30 min or max 5 sessions on Initial Touch), Must Initiate (enter reward tray to start trial, complete 100 trials in 60 min), Punish Incorrect (time-out for incorrect touch, complete 100 trials in under 60 min with at least 70% correct). Modifications include removing auditory correct tone, changing reward from pellet to liquid, increasing trials per session, reducing ITI to 5 s.

nodes.title: Visual Discrimination (VD) Task
nodes.action: Train mice to discriminate between two visual stimuli (single large white circle and four small white circles). Present two stimuli per trial; reward correct selection. Require mice to complete 100 trials within 60 min and achieve at least 80% correct. Use correction trials repeating incorrect choice until correct choice is made to prevent side bias.

nodes.title: Reversal Learning Task
nodes.action: After VD task acquisition, reverse reward contingencies so previously unrewarded stimulus is now correct. Test mice until they reach 80% correct or a maximum of 20 sessions to assess behavioral flexibility.

nodes.title: Open Field Locomotor Activity Test
nodes.action: Place mice individually in square Perspex chambers (27 × 27 × 20 cm) equipped with infrared beams to track body position.
